apps.description: Frees up storage by clearing out the junk files apps leave behind.
highlights: Finds temporary files, logs, thumbnails and empty folders
Pick exactly what gets cleaned, and whitelist what stays
Open source, with no ads or trackers
apps.pitch: Give your phone a tidy-up. It sweeps out the junk files apps quietly leave behind.

setup.title: Allow access to all files
setup.detail: It needs this to find and clear junk files across your storage. Without it, it can't see them.

setup.title: Allow notifications
setup.detail: Lets scheduled cleans tell you what they cleared.

guide.settingsWhere: its Settings (the gear on the main screen)
tips: Turn on Auto Whitelist, so folders other apps rely on are protected automatically
Look through Whitelist before your first clean, and add anything you want kept
Clean on boot or Hourly Clean keep things tidy without opening the app
Leave Delete .apk files off if you keep app installers around
guide.backup: open Settings and tap Export Data
guide.restore: open Settings, tap Import Data and pick the file you saved

apps.description: Clears the cache of all your apps in one go, no root needed.
highlights: Clears cached data app by app, automatically
Uses Android's accessibility service to do the tapping for you
Open source, with no ads or trackers
apps.pitch: Every app's cache, gone in one go. Spring cleaning without the elbow grease.

setup.title: Turn on its accessibility service
setup.detail: Android only lets system apps clear other apps' caches in one go, so it uses this to tap Clear cache in each app's settings for you. It's open source, so what it does with it can be checked.

setup.title: Allow usage access
setup.detail: It needs this to see your apps and how much cache each one holds before it can clean them.

tips: Start with User Apps rather than All Apps, and untick anything you'd rather leave alone
Tap the floating button during a clean to stop it early
If you'd rather it isn't left on, tap Stop Accessibility service in the app when you're done

apps.description: Signs you in to your Google account in apps that need it, without Google Play services.
highlights: Google account sign-in for apps that rely on it
A light, open-source stand-in for Google Play services
Other apps in the Krate may list it as a requirement

setup.title: Let it run in the background
setup.detail: Apps that sign in or get notifications through it stop working properly if Android puts it to sleep.

setup.title: Allow notifications
setup.detail: So it can ask when an app wants to use your account.

setup.title: Add your Google account
setup.detail: Only if you want to sign in to apps that use it. Tap Open on this page and go to Accounts.

guide.settingsWhere: microG Settings (the Open button on this page)
tips: Self-Check shows at a glance whether everything is set up
Keep Cloud Messaging on for notifications from apps that rely on it
Krate installs the build without a launcher icon, so Open on this page is the way in. microG's own hide-icon switch isn't needed, and it can swap in a newer test build

apps.description: A free, open-source manga reader for Android.
highlights: Read from many sources through extensions
Track your reading with AniList, MyAnimeList and more
Download chapters to read offline, with backups built in
apps.pitch: Your manga shelf, in your pocket. Read, collect and pick up right where you left off.

setup.title: Choose a storage location
setup.detail: On first launch Mihon asks for a folder. Downloads and backups are saved there.

setup.title: Allow it to install apps
setup.detail: Sources come as extensions, and Mihon installs them itself. Without this, there's nothing to read from.

setup.title: Allow notifications
setup.detail: For library updates and finished downloads.

setup.title: Let it run in the background
setup.detail: Keeps long library updates, downloads and backup restores from being cut off.

walkthrough.title: Say hello to Mihon
walkthrough.detail: Mihon opens with a few welcome pages. Pick a folder for its downloads when it asks, and say yes to installing extensions. Finish those pages first, because the store can only be added after them.

walkthrough.title: Add the extension store
walkthrough.detail: Mihon starts with an empty shelf. Extensions are its sources: they bring the manga, and their updates show up in Mihon too. This store, from the Keiyoushi project, is where most of them come from. Tap the button and Krate adds it for you.

walkthrough.title: Pick your sources
walkthrough.detail: Open Browse in Mihon, then Extensions, and install the sources you like. When one has an update, it shows up right there. Prefer to add the store yourself? In Browse > Extensions, open the menu, choose Extension stores and paste the address from the last step.

tips: Data and storage: set Automatic backup frequency so a backup is always there
Browse > Extensions is where you add the sources you read from
Tracking connects AniList, MyAnimeList and others, so progress follows you
guide.backup: open More > Settings > Data and storage and tap Create backup
guide.restore: open More > Settings > Data and storage, tap Restore backup and pick the file
